issues.description: The problem statement contains conflicting information about the type of the Farm.animals attribute: the UML shows animals as a List<Animal>, but the textual Part 3 explicitly requires a Set implemented with a HashSet. The provided solution implements animals as a List (ArrayList). This mismatch between the problem text/UML and the solution (and the ambiguity inside the problem statement itself) can confuse students about whether they must use a Set/HashSet (and enforce uniqueness) or a List/ArrayList.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the requirement consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement and UML to require a List/ArrayList (remove the 'Set/HashSet' wording in Part 3), or (B) change the solution (and template) to use a Set<Animal> and instantiate it with new HashSet<>() in the no-arg constructor, and update getter/setter signatures to use Set<Animal>. If uniqueness is intended, prefer option (B) and modify Farm.java to: private Set<Animal> animals; import java.util.HashSet; import java.util.Set; public Farm() { this.animals = new HashSet<>(); } and adjust related methods accordingly.
